blind.description: A set of four Egyptian-style canopic jars arranged in a 2x2 grid inside a low wooden tray or crate. Each jar has a rounded beige ceramic body accented with a colored decorative stripe (blue, red, gold, green) around the neck or belly. The lids are sculpted as traditional protective heads: a human head (Imsety), a baboon head (Hapi), a jackal head (Duamutef), and a falcon head (Qebehsenuef). The surfaces are clean, smooth, and stylized with crisp textures.
blind.from_above: A square wooden frame containing four round jar lids arranged in a 2x2 formation, showing the tops of the sculpted animal and human head lids.
blind.extra_base_or_ground: low square wooden tray/stand with corner feet
blind.height_vs_figure: About 1/4 the height of the figure (around 1.3 to 1.5 feet tall) and about 1.5 feet wide across the wooden tray.
